title: Inspection Photos & Hold Points
short_answer: What to photograph before you cover it, how to tag it, and when covering without a clear is how you buy tear-out.
summary: What to photograph before you cover it, how to tag it, and when covering without a clear is how you buy tear-out.
plain_words: If an inspector or GC needs to see a layer, and you covered it, you own the reopen. Photo first. Rated walls, shaftliner, firestop, insulation before the second side, and resilient channel are the usual hold points.
when_to_use: Before covering any rated assembly layer or firestop
Before second-side board on insulated or shaft walls
Before resilient channel disappears behind board
After a failed inspection — before any repair or cover-up
prerequisites: Know the hold points on this assembly — ask the lead if unsure
Fire Walls & Shaftwall and Firestopping procedures reviewed

tools.name: Room or grid label habit (frame or filename)

steps.title: Know the hold points
steps.body: Know the hold points on this assembly before you start covering — ask the lead if unsure.

steps.title: Photo
steps.body: Wide (where you are) + close (the detail). Include a room or grid label in the frame or filename habit the lead uses.

steps.title: Typical set
steps.body: Base layer / shaftliner, firestop at head-of-wall and penetrations, insulation before 2nd side, RC/hat channel before board.

steps.title: Wait for clear
steps.body: Do not cover until the lead (and GC/inspector when required) clears — Job Check "ready" is not a substitute for a failed inspection.

steps.title: Failed inspection
steps.body: Stop, photo the red tag / note, call the lead. Tear-out vs repair is their call with the office.

warnings.title: Cover without a clear
warnings.body: If an inspector or GC needed to see a layer and you covered it, you own the reopen. Photo first; wait for lead and inspector clearance when required.

warnings.title: Job Check is not inspection clearance
warnings.body: Flipping a stage chip to ready does not replace a failed inspection or a required GC hold-point sign-off.

quality_checks.prompt: Hold points for this assembly identified before cover-up starts
Wide + close photos with room/grid context before cover
Lead (and inspector when required) cleared before cover
Failed inspection photographed and escalated before repair

common_mistakes.title: Cover to keep schedule
common_mistakes.wrong: Board over shaftliner or firestop because the GC is pushing
common_mistakes.why: Tear-out cost lands on whoever covered without proof

common_mistakes.title: Job Check as inspection substitute
common_mistakes.wrong: Mark Hanging ready while inspection is still open
common_mistakes.right: Separate inspection clearance from board updates
common_mistakes.why: A failed tag means stop — not a chip update

common_mistakes.title: Close-up only photos
common_mistakes.wrong: Detail photo with no room or grid context
common_mistakes.right: Wide + close; label in frame or filename habit
common_mistakes.why: Useless for disputes without location proof

common_mistakes.title: Repair after failed inspection without lead
common_mistakes.wrong: Cover the red tag and keep going
common_mistakes.right: Stop, photo tag, call lead — tear-out vs repair is their call
common_mistakes.why: Office needs authority on rated-work rework
